package_info.why_malicious: The 3CXDesktopApp was compromised in a supply chain attack, where legitimate signed installers were modified to include a malicious ffmpeg.dll. This DLL is sideloaded by the main application and decrypts and loads a second-stage payload from d3dcompiler_47.dll. The decrypted payload executes shellcode that connects to attacker-controlled infrastructure to download additional malicious code, enabling remote code execution, persistence, and potential data exfiltration.

required_permissions: filesystem (to load DLLs and read encrypted payload)
network (for subsequent payload download by loaded shellcode)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious ffmpeg.dll (SHA256: 7986bbaee8940da11ce089383521ab420c443ab7b15ed42aed91fd31ce833896) is sideloaded by 3CXDesktopApp.exe and contains code to decrypt and load an encrypted blob from d3dcompiler_47.dll.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At application launch, the trojanized ffmpeg.dll is loaded by 3CXDesktopApp.exe, decrypts an embedded payload from d3dcompiler_47.dll, and executes the decrypted shellcode in memory, enabling the application to perform unauthorized actions such as downloading further malicious payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: A legitimate media library DLL (ffmpeg.dll) should not perform decryption or in-memory code execution, especially when sideloaded by a signed application.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal ffmpeg.dll is used for media processing and should not contain code to decrypt or execute additional payloads from other DLLs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: DLL sideloading can be used for plugin architectures, but not for decrypting and executing code from another DLL. Legitimate plugins do not perform in-memory code injection.
key_indicators: Sideloading of a non-standard or modified ffmpeg.dll by 3CXDesktopApp.exe
ffmpeg.dll containing code to decrypt and execute payloads from d3dcompiler_47.dll

execution_context.trigger: After ffmpeg.dll execution (runtime, post-decryption of payload)
required_permissions: network (to connect to external repositories and download files)
filesystem (to read encrypted blob and potentially write further payloads)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Encrypted blob within d3dcompiler_47.dll (SHA256: 11be1803e2e307b647a8a7e02d128335c448ff741bf06bf52b332e0bbf423b03) contains shellcode that attempts to download ICO files from GitHub, extract URIs, and download further payloads.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After ffmpeg.dll decrypts and executes the shellcode from d3dcompiler_47.dll, the shellcode initiates outbound network connections to remote repositories (such as GitHub), downloads ICO files containing hidden URIs, extracts these URIs, and retrieves additional malicious payloads for in-memory execution, resulting in further compromise of the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: A standard Microsoft DLL (d3dcompiler_47.dll) should not contain encrypted blobs with shellcode designed to download and execute additional code from the internet.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: d3dcompiler_47.dll is expected to provide Direct3D shader compilation functionality and should not contain or execute any shellcode or perform network operations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Encrypted blobs may be used in legitimate software for DRM or anti-tampering, but not for downloading and executing code from external sources.
key_indicators: Presence of an encrypted payload within d3dcompiler_47.dll
Shellcode that establishes outbound network connections to download files
Use of ICO files to conceal download URIs for further payload retrieval

attack_chain.action: User installs or launches the trojanized 3CXDesktopApp, which loads the malicious ffmpeg.dll via DLL sideloading.
attack_chain.leads_to: Decryption and execution of payload from d3dcompiler_47.dll

attack_chain.action: ffmpeg.dll decrypts and loads shellcode from d3dcompiler_47.dll, executing it in memory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Shellcode attempts to download further payloads from attacker infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Shellcode connects to remote repositories (e.g., GitHub), downloads ICO files, extracts URIs, and retrieves additional malicious payloads for execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of attacker-controlled code and potential data exfiltration or further compromise

behavioral_signatures: DLL sideloading of non-standard or modified DLLs (e.g., ffmpeg.dll) by signed applications such as 3CXDesktopApp.exe
Decryption and in-memory execution of code from secondary DLLs (e.g., d3dcompiler_47.dll)
Runtime network connections from 3CXDesktopApp processes to download additional payloads, especially from GitHub or similar repositories
Use of ICO files or other non-standard file types to conceal download URIs for further payload retrieval
file_indicators: Presence of ffmpeg.dll (SHA256: 7986bbaee8940da11ce089383521ab420c443ab7b15ed42aed91fd31ce833896) in the 3CXDesktopApp application directory
Presence of d3dcompiler_47.dll (SHA256: 11be1803e2e307b647a8a7e02d128335c448ff741bf06bf52b332e0bbf423b03) with an embedded encrypted payload
Unusually large or modified DLLs (ffmpeg.dll, d3dcompiler_47.dll) in application folders compared to official distributions
network_indicators: Connections to attacker-controlled domains such as akamaicontainer[.]com, akamaitechcloudservices[.]com, azuredeploystore[.]com, azureonlinecloud[.]com, azureonlinestorage[.]com, dunamistrd[.]com, glcloudservice[.]com, journalide[.]org, msedgepackageinfo[.]com, msstorageazure[.]com, msstorageboxes[.]com, officeaddons[.]com, officestoragebox[.]com, pbxcloudeservices[.]com, pbxphonenetwork[.]com, pbxsources[.]com, qwepoi123098[.]com, sbmsa[.]wikisourceslabs[.]com, visualstudiofactory[.]com, zacharryblogs[.]com, convieneonline[.]com, soyoungjun[.]com
Attempts to download ICO files from GitHub or similar code repositories
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for DLL sideloading activity, particularly where 3CXDesktopApp.exe loads non-standard or modified DLLs (such as ffmpeg.dll) that are not part of the official distribution. Inspect these DLLs for the presence of encrypted blobs or code that performs decryption and in-memory execution. Monitor network traffic from 3CXDesktopApp processes for connections to known malicious domains or attempts to download files (especially ICO files) from external repositories. Flag the presence of the listed malicious hashes or unexpected modifications to d3dcompiler_47.dll and ffmpeg.dll in the application directory. Compare DLL file sizes and hashes against known-good versions to identify tampering.
